text:
maya: Customer on Dedicated reporting SSO failure after their IdP key rollover. They started seeing 403s at our ACS endpoint this morning. Can someone triage? :eyes:

maya: Quick repro from their side (sanitized):
```
POST /saml/acs HTTP/1.1
Host: app.redwood-inference.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
SAMLResponse=FZk... (base64)
RelayState=xyz
```
Response: 403 InvalidRecipient - received recipient=https://acme.example.com/saml/callback expected=https://app.redwood-inference.com/saml/acs

raj: Do we have the customer's IdP metadata URL? Also what tenant config do we have for ACS hostnames?

maya: Metadata URL: https://idp.acme.example.com/metadata.xml (they updated it post-rotation). They say they pushed a new cert + metadata. I fetched the metadata and saw two KeyDescriptor nodes; the signing cert shows an intermediate chain that includes an expired cross-signed cert (dates look odd). Snippet: 
```xml
<KeyDescriptor use="signing">
  <KeyInfo>
    <X509Data>
      <X509Certificate>MIIF...AB (truncated)</X509Certificate>
    </X509Data>
  </KeyInfo>
</KeyDescriptor>
```

oliver: The 403 text (InvalidRecipient) suggests our SP recipient/audience check is failing — i.e., the SAML Assertion recipient doesn't match the ACS we expect. Is this multi-tenant where IdPs can send back a tenant-hosted ACS?

maya: Yes, acme uses a custom domain for SSO callbacks (acme.example.com). Historically our proxy canonicalized and forwarded Host headers so we accepted that. After a recent proxy tweak we normalize the ACS host to app.redwood-inference.com for routing, which may be causing a mismatch between the Assertion Recipient and our expected value.

raj: Can you paste the assertion SubjectConfirmationData/Recipient value (sanitized)?

maya: From their decoded SAMLAssertion: 
```
<SubjectConfirmationData Recipient="https://acme.example.com/saml/callback" NotOnOrAfter="2026-04-01T12:03:10Z" />
```

maya: Also note their RelayState is preserved by the CDN, but the edge rewrites Host to the origin host for cache hits in some regions — I'm suspicious the edge is rewriting the Host header when we do origin pull, so the recipient the IdP put in the assertion differs from what our SP checks (we check against canonical tenant ACS).

oliver: Quick tests: can you curl our ACS with Host: acme.example.com and without and paste responses? That will show whether request normalization is changing behavior. Example: 
```
curl -v -H "Host: acme.example.com" https://app.redwood-inference.com/saml/acs
```

maya: Ran both. With Host: acme.example.com -> 403 InvalidRecipient (body shows recipient https://acme.example.com/saml/callback). With default Host -> 403 but expected recipient=https://app.redwood-inference.com/saml/acs. So the check compares assertion Recipient to the tenant-configured accepted recipients list; since the tenant has a custom ACS host we should accept both, but our recent deploy tightened validation to only allow canonical host.

raj: That aligns. We pushed a change that tightened recipient validation for a security hardening task (ticket INF-2145) but didn't register tenants using custom domains. We need a short-term workaround and a long-term fix.

idp-bot: metadata-fetch: fetched idp.acme.example.com/metadata.xml at 2026-03-16T09:12:10Z, signature OK, certs present (one cert chain includes intermediate with expiry 2024-11-10).

lisa: For enterprise customer acme: high-impact. Recommended immediate steps: 1) Confirm with customer whether they can switch IdP to send Recipient=https://app.redwood-inference.com/saml/acs (preferred). 2) If they need immediate access, we can add acme.example.com to allowed recipients for that tenant temporarily (requires config change and security review). 3) Schedule rollback or targeted relax for the validation rule for only their tenant while we properly roll out canonicalization/host-preserve fix.

oliver: Security note — if we relax recipient checks, limit to the exact tenant and require a signed admin approval emailed to security@redwood.com. Also we should check the IdP's cert chain (the expired intermediate): if their chain includes expired certs, IdP should fix chain; we may still accept signature if leaf cert is valid and chain can be built to a trusted root, but expired intermediates are often the root cause for some SP libraries.

maya: Customer prefers quick access. They can confirm admin approval. I'll ask them to send signed approval and request they rotate IdP metadata to remove expired intermediate or supply full chain correctly. Meanwhile, can engineering add a tenant-scoped recipient allowlist toggle?

raj: I'll own the engineering change. Plan: add tenant-scoped config that maps allowed Recipient values (pulled from tenant settings) and a safety flag to require admin-signed approval for on-demand toggles. I'll coordinate with security for the approval flow. Target: hotfix within 2-3 hours if oncall approves.

lisa: I'll open an incident and flag as P1 for support+security+eng. Notify account manager and request written approval from customer. :lock: :phone:

maya: Thanks — I'll message the customer for approval and post their reply here.

(reacts: maya :thumbsup:, oliver :eyes:)
